citation.title: Open-source LLMs for text annotation: a practical guide for model setting and fine-tuning
citation.venue_or_publisher: Journal of Computational Social Science 8, 17 (2025); published online 18 December 2024

question: How well do open-source language models (LLaMA, FLAN) classify text for political science tasks (relevance, topic, stance, frames), compared with GPT-3.5/GPT-4 and crowd-workers, and which choices (zero-shot, few-shot, fine-tuning, temperature, amount of annotation) matter.
data: Four datasets, 9,777 texts in total: 2,978 tweets on content moderation (2020-2021); 3,006 tweets by US Congress members (2017-2022); 2,480 newspaper articles on content moderation (2020-2021, LexisNexis); 1,313 tweets from January 2023. Eleven annotation tasks. Gold standard: three trained political science students. Comparison: Amazon MTurk workers (two per text).
method: Each model's labels were compared with the trained annotators' labels (accuracy, intercoder agreement, per-class precision/recall/F1). Zero-shot, few-shot (chain-of-thought examples) and fine-tuning (training sets of 50 to 1,500 texts, at least 15% held out for evaluation) were compared for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA-1/2/3 and FLAN-T5. Texts on which the two trained annotators disagreed were left out of the accuracy calculation. Temperature 0.2 and the default were compared; fine-tuning runs used 0.0.

definitions.definition: Share of correct predictions, with the trained human annotations as gold standard, counting only texts both annotators agreed on.
definitions.quote: using trained human annotations as our gold standard and considering only texts that both annotators agreed upon

definitions.definition: Share of instances for which two annotators in a group (or two runs of the same model) give the same class.
definitions.quote: intercoder agreement, measured as the percentage of instances for which both annotators in a given group report the same class

definitions.definition: The model generalises to tasks it has not seen, with no labelled examples.
definitions.quote: Zero-Shot Learning enables models to generalize to hitherto unseen tasks without the requirement for labeled examples

definitions.definition: A minimal set of annotated examples is used to adapt the model to a new task.
definitions.quote: Few-Shot Learning leverages a minimal set of annotated instances to adapt the model to new tasks

definitions.definition: Retraining the model on a specialised dataset to improve task-specific performance.
definitions.quote: fine-tuning constitutes the retraining of LLMs on a specialized, domain-specific dataset to augment task-specific performance

definitions.definition: Whether a tweet is about content moderation, or in a separate task about politics.
definitions.quote: relevance: whether a tweet is about content moderation or, in a separate task, about politics

proxies.indicator: Agreement with labels from three trained annotators working from the same codebook, counting only texts on which both annotators agreed.
proxies.quote: each of the students operated independently and systematically annotated the dataset task by task, adhering to a uniform codebook and shared procedural guidelines

proxies.indicator: Intercoder agreement between two runs of the same model, at default and lowered temperature.
proxies.quote: We conducted two sets of annotations for each temperature value to compute LLM’s intercoder agreement.

proxies.indicator: Precision, recall and F1 per class, used so that models are not biased towards the majority class.
proxies.quote: we calculated each class’s precision, recall, and F1 score

proxies.concept: contamination of results by training data
proxies.indicator: A new sample of tweets from 2023, after the models' training cut-off, added so that the models are not merely reproducing training texts.
proxies.quote: to address the concern that LLMs might be merely reproducing texts that could have been part of their training data

findings.claim: Zero-shot GPT-3.5 beat crowd-workers by about 25 percentage points on average (finding of the earlier study this one extends).
findings.quote: the zero-shot accuracy of GPT\(-\)3.5 exceeds that of crowd workers by about 25 percentage points on average
findings.page: Choosing the training approach: zero-shot versus few-shot

findings.claim: Few-shot prompting gave mixed results: some tasks gained, some lost, with no pattern by task complexity, model or data type.
findings.quote: In our tests, few-shot results are mixed, some tasks benefited from it and some lost performance.
findings.page: Choosing the training approach: zero-shot versus few-shot

findings.claim: Lowering the temperature raised agreement between two runs of the same model (GPT-3.5 zero-shot from 91.7% to 97.6%; LLaMA-1 HuggingChat from 46.7% to 84.8%).
findings.quote: GPT\(-\)3.5’s average intercoder agreement increased from 91.7% to 97.6% when the temperature was reduced from 1 to 0.2 in the zero-shot setting

findings.claim: In almost all tasks, lower temperature raised run-to-run agreement without lowering accuracy; one exception was the relevance task on 2020-2021 tweets.
findings.quote: in almost all annotation tasks, lower temperature setting for GPT-3.5 and HuggingChat increases the intercoder agreement rate without decreasing the accuracy

findings.claim: No model was best on all 11 tasks; only GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 beat crowd-workers on all 11.
findings.quote: no LLM outperforms others across all 11 annotation tasks; (2) only GPT-4 and GPT\(-\)3.5 outperform MTurkers in all 11 annotation tasks
findings.page: Model selection: proprietary versus open-source LLMs

findings.claim: Open-source models are not consistently the best choice but generally beat crowd-workers and approach GPT-3.5.
findings.quote: while open-source LLMs are not consistently the superior choice, they generally outperform crowd-sourced annotations and are approaching the performance levels of GPT 3.5
findings.page: Model selection: proprietary versus open-source LLMs

findings.claim: Fine-tuned FLAN-T5 (XL) matched or exceeded zero-shot GPT-3.5 on all tasks and datasets except one; accuracy generally rose with the amount of fine-tuning data.
findings.quote: FLAN-T5 (XL) matches or even surpasses GPT-3.5’s zero-shot performance across all tasks and datasets (except one task)
findings.page: Annotation size: how much annotation is enough for fine-tuning?

findings.claim: Fine-tuning GPT-3.5 with 50 examples raised average accuracy by 15.7%; open-source models improved more gradually.
findings.quote: it registers an average accuracy increase of 15.7 %, which further escalates to 19.1 % when the training set comprises 100 cases
findings.page: Annotation size: how much annotation is enough for fine-tuning?

findings.claim: Authors recommend (advice, not a measured result): always have a human expert annotate 100-250 items to measure model accuracy on a new dataset or task.
findings.quote: Always manually annotate 100-250 data points to measure the accuracy of LLMs, specailly If working on a new dataset or task.
findings.page: Choosing the training approach: zero-shot versus few-shot

findings.claim: Authors recommend (advice): validate model output against human experts, run the model at least twice per task and report average accuracy and intercoder agreement, and set temperature to zero or low.
findings.quote: always validate the output of LLMs by human expert evaluation; (4) run LLMs at least twice per task and report average accuracy and intercoder agreement

findings.claim: Authors recommend (advice): annotate 250-500 items and use half for fine-tuning and half for accuracy testing.
findings.quote: manually annotate 250-500 data points and use half for fine-tuning and half for accuracy testing

limitations.point: Results should not be generalised across all annotation tasks or datasets; researchers should run their own evaluation on their own data.
limitations.quote: these results should not be broadly generalized across all forms of text annotation tasks or datasets

limitations.point: The mixed results (e.g. few-shot) could not be explained; the authors list possible factors but did not test them.
limitations.quote: we could not find any conclusive pattern
limitations.page: Choosing the training approach: zero-shot versus few-shot

limitations.point: Models' training data and internal workings are not transparent, so why a given input gives a given output cannot be explained; caution advised where explainability matters.
limitations.quote: we advise researchers to exercise caution when employing these models in domains where interpretability and explainability are critical
limitations.page: A note on explainability of LLMs performance

limitations.point: Fine-tuned models may still fall short of the accuracy a specialised application needs; complex tasks need substantial high-quality training data.
limitations.quote: Despite fine-tuning, it remains possible that the model’s performance may not meet the thresholds required for specific specialized applications.
limitations.page: Annotation size: how much annotation is enough for fine-tuning?

limitations.point: Tasks are social-media and news text classification (content moderation, US politics); none classifies organisations or uses web pages as input. The gold standard is three student annotators, and no agreement statistic among them (e.g. kappa) is reported in the text; agreement with MTurk is by percentage only.
Supplementary Appendix (full task instructions S1, prompts S2, extra figures) was not in the text file; figure values were not readable.
